text:
Sam H.: Heads up — design question: when an automatic fallback switches model variants for a rollout, do we create a mandatory audit record only, or also surface an approval/override in the console?
Aisha P.: I'd vote for audit + optional approval. Most customers want traceability but not constant human ops.
Liam C.: To add: some customers will want an approval gate if fallback affects >X% of traffic or if latency goes up.
Eva R.: Agree. We should support thresholds: error-rate, latency, and dropped tokens. If the trigger breaches threshold AND impact > traffic_pct -> require manual approval.
Sam H.: Good point. How would that look in the UI? Quick mock idea: a toast + banner on the rollout page showing "automatic fallback engaged" with a button: "Pause auto-fallback / Open audit".
Aisha P.: UX thought: default to "auto-fallback allowed" for self-serve, and enable "approval required" as a policy per project/account. Avoid nagging notifications.
Liam C.: From infra side, we need an immutable audit record for every fallback decision with metadata: timestamp, rule, signal values, old_variant, new_variant, trace_id, and the evaluation window.
Jae M.: +1. Also include the exact decision graph so you can replay the conditions later. We should store the policy snapshot that evaluated true.
rollout-bot: Deploy check: fallback-policy v2 evaluated on 1768004280 -> rule matched (latency > 750ms on p99).
Eva R.: roll-out telemetry must link to a trace. We can surface a clickable trace_id that opens trace in APM. If no trace, show sample request logs.
Sam H.: How about notifications? Slack/email/webhook when fallback requires approval, and a quieter log entry for automatic-only changes.
Aisha P.: For the console, propose a compact event timeline on the rollout page: [start rollout] -> [metric drift] -> [fallback triggered auto] -> [audit recorded] -> [manual override]. Each item expandable to details.
Liam C.: Implementation constraints: automatic fallback must not block the request path; decision should be computed asynchronously with a TTL'd cache so routing can continue even during evaluation spikes.
Sam H.: We should allow customers to configure two degrade modes: "soft switch" (traffic gradually redirected with canary) and "hard switch" (immediate). Soft switch also writes more granular audit events.
Jae M.: Proposal for policy schema (example):
```json
{
  "policy_name": "p99_latency_fallback",
  "triggers": [
    {"metric": "p99_latency_ms", "operator": ">", "value": 750, "window_sec": 300},
    {"metric": "error_rate", "operator": ">", "value": 0.03, "window_sec": 300}
  ],
  "traffic_threshold_pct": 10,
  "degrade_mode": "soft",
  "approval_required": true
}
```
Eva R.: Nice. We also need a tamper-proof audit id (UUID) and retention policy. Legal may ask for 1 year or longer for some customers.
Aisha P.: UX: when approval_required=true, show a single-button "Approve fallback" with a confirmation modal that surfaces the event details + links to traces and sample outputs. Include who approved and why (free text).
Liam C.: Security: only certain roles should be able to approve. Map to IAM roles and enforce via backend.
Sam H.: One more: costs. If fallback increases token usage, show estimated incremental cost in the audit UI so reviewers can decide.
Jae M.: OK next steps: I'll draft a lightweight API contract for the audit events (immutable), and a console wireframe for the timeline + approval modal.
Aisha P.: I'll mock the notification wording and suggested defaults for self-serve vs enterprise.
Liam C.: I'll prototype the TTL caching + async evaluator so routing latency isn't impacted.
Sam H.: Great. Can we reconvene in 48h with prototypes? @everyone please drop any hard constraints now. :thumbsup:
Eva R.: FYI: enterprise customers have asked for configurable retention and SOC logs. Will surface in next doc.
